name: 2-Step Chicken
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://myplate.food/recipes/2-step-chicken
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1 can (10.75 ounces) reduced-sodium cream of chicken soup

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in a skillet at a medium-high setting.
Add chicken and cook for ten minutes.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Stir the soup and water together in the skillet and heat it to a boil.
Return the chicken to the skillet.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer for an additional 10 minutes, or until the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 165 degrees F.

notes.text: This recipe uses reduced-sodium cream of chicken soup.

name: 20-Minute Chicken Creole
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013807/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/20-minute-chicken-creole
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1 can (14.5 ounces) no salt added diced tomatoes

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat pan over medium-high heat (350 degrees F in an electric skillet). Add vegetable oil and chicken and cook until the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 165 degrees F (3-5 minutes).
Reduce heat to medium (300 degrees F in electric skillet).
Add tomatoes with juice, chili sauce*, green pepper, celery, onion, garlic, basil, parsley, and cayenne pepper..
Bring to a boil; reduce heat to low and simmer, covered for 10-15 minutes.
Serve over hot, cooked rice or whole wheat pasta.
1 can (8 ounces) tomato sauce
1 Tablespoon vinegar
1 teaspoon packed brown sugar
1 teaspoon chili powder

name: 3-Can Chili
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013810/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/3-can-chili
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can (15.5 ounces) low-sodium black beans, undrained (or pinto, kidney, or red beans)
1 can (15.2 ounces) reduced sodium corn, drained (or 10-oz package of frozen corn)
1 can (14.5 ounces) low-sodium crushed tomatoes, undrained
1 teaspoon chili powder (or more, to taste)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place the contents of all 3 cans into a pan.
Add chili powder to taste.
Stir to mix.
Continue to stir over medium heat until heated thoroughly.
Refrigerate leftovers.

name: 5 A Day Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013814/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/5-day-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups chopped green peppers (or red, yellow, or orange peppers)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash all of the vegetables and mix them together in a large mixing bowl.
Top this colorful meal with the nonfat or low-fat dressing of your choice.

notes.text: The dressing is not included in the nutritional analysis. Each serving = 5 cups of vegetables (Eight 5-A-Day servings).

name: Ambrosia
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013818/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/ambrosia
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can (20 ounces) pineapple chunks in juice, drained

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain pineapple and oranges. Use juice as beverage.
Combine fruit with marshmallows and coconut.
Fold in yogurt.
Chill.
Serve.

name: Angel Food Cake
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013822/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/angel-food-cake
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F. In a large mixing bowl, beat the egg whites until they are foamy.
Add the cream of tartar and beat until stiff, but not dry. Gradually beat in the sugar
Add the vanilla and salt and then gently fold in the flour.
Pour the mix into an angel food tubular 10-inch pan and bake for 1 hour and 15 minutes, or until the top is nicely browned.

name: Anytime Pizza
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013824/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/anytime-pizza
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 mini baguette or Italian bread, about 9" long (split lengthwise, or 2 split English muffins)
1/2 cup part-skim mozzarella or cheddar cheese, shredded
1/4 cup mushrooms, fresh or canned, sliced

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Toast the bread or English muffin until slightly brown.
Top bread or muffin with pizza sauce, vegetables and low-fat cheese.
Sprinkle with Italian seasoning as desired.
Return bread to toaster oven (or regular oven preheated to 350 degrees F).
Heat until cheese melts.
serving_size: 1 slice, 1 English muffin or 1/2 of recipe

name: Apple Banana Salad with Peanuts
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013851/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/apple-banana-salad-peanuts
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 1/2 medium apples, sliced (14 oz. of sliced apples)

steps: Whisk together dressing ingredients.
Slice bananas.
In a large salad bowl, toss mixed greens, banana and apple slices, peanuts, and dressing.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with 8 ounce non-fat milk and one slice of rustic whole-grain bread. Tips on how to select and store bananas:

name: Apple Cake
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013859/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/apple-cake
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 10 tablespoons unsalted butter (1 full stick + 2 tablespoons)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F.
Beat butter with sugar until creamy.
Add eggs one at a time, beating until well blended.
Add flour, baking powder, and lemon rind, beat 4 minutes.
Pour into greased 9-inch spring-form pan.
Arrange the apples on the batter, sprinkle with 2 teaspoons sugar.
Bake 1 hour at 350 degrees F in preheated oven.
Remove from pan, brush apples with jam, cool.

name: Apple Carrot Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013902/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/apple-carrot-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 pound lean pork, cut into chunks
4 medium apples, cored and quartered (with skin)
4 large carrots, peeled and cut into chunks

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large pot over high heat, combine all ingredients, bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to medium and simmer until soup reduces to about 8 cups of liquid, about 3 to 4 hours.
Skim fat from surface and serve.
Store leftover soup covered in refrigerator for up to 3 days.

name: Apple & Chicken Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013848/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/apple-chicken-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 chicken breasts (skinless, cooked, diced, about 2 cups)
16 lettuce leaves (Bibb, Romaine, green or red leaf)

steps: Cut apples in quarters; remove core and chop.
In a medium size bowl, mix all ingredients, except lettuce.
To serve, arrange lettuce on serving plates top with apple and chicken salad.

notes.text: Weekly Menu Planning Tip: When you're planning a dinner with chicken cook up extra chicken breast and refrigerate for later use in this salad. Serve with 8 ounce non-fat milk and 1 slice rustic whole grain bread.

name: Apple Chunk Cake
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013908/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/apple-chunk-cake
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 cup vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
4 cups apples, divided (2 cups chopped into chunks, 2 cups sliced)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
In a large bowl, mix sugar, oil and eggs together. Beat well.
In a separate bowl, combine flour, salt, cinnamon, and baking soda. Add to egg batter and mix well.
Add 2 cups of apple chunks and applesauce to the batter. Stir to combine.
Coat an 8x8-inch baking pan with vegetable oil spray and pour in batter.
Bake until done, about 1 hour.
Place 2 cups of apple slices on top of apple cake and serve.

notes.text: Batter will be very thick. This is normal.
